rounds.fact: IMDb started in 1990 as a hobbyist mailing list of movie trivia before becoming a website, and is still one of the oldest continuously running sites on the entire internet.
BuzzFeed started in 2006 as an experiment in tracking what content spreads virally online, well before its listicle format became one of the most imitated web formats of the 2010s.
Woot's entire business model was selling exactly one product per day until it sold out, a simple gimmick that built a cult following before Amazon eventually bought the company.
Suck.com pioneered a sarcastic, link-heavy, first-person writing style that influenced blog voice for years, despite the site itself shutting down back in 2001.
Gawker built its identity on gossipy, irreverent media and tech coverage, and its comment sections were an early influential experiment in giving readers real visibility on a media site.
